title: A Protocol for the Safehouse
premise: Jude Thornbury, a deniable private security contractor, is hired to escort a client on a routine regional flight when the aircraft's records vanish mid-flight and the plane lands at an airfield that officially does not exist. Among the survivors is Vess, a defector carrying proof that the flight's disappearance was engineered as bait to lure Jude's employer into exposing its network. As border checkpoint shift schedules tighten around them, Jude must choose between the duty that has defined their life and the found family of strangers the crash leaves them responsible for. The story ends with Jude burning their own contract identity to smuggle Vess across during a checkpoint change, surviving the exchange but losing everything except the people they saved.
about_author: Bram Nystrom is a former logistics coordinator for humanitarian convoys who writes thrillers drawn from the paperwork of disappearances. They live near a border they have crossed more times than they can count.

chapters.title: Manifest of One
chapters.summary: Jude Thornbury's POV. Jude takes a low-attribution job escorting a nervous client onto a regional charter, noting oddities in the passenger manifest: one name too many. The emotional beat is professional detachment beginning to crack as Jude senses the job is wrong before anything visibly goes wrong.

chapters.title: Squawk Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Jude aboard the plane and their handler Mara on the ground. Mid-flight, every digital record of the aircraft evaporates; transponders go dark, booking systems show no such flight. The beat is creeping dread — the world quietly deleting them while they are still in it.

chapters.title: The Airfield That Isn't
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The plane diverts to an unlisted airstrip and lands hard. Survivors include Vess, the extra passenger, who claims the disappearance was manufactured. Jude must secure the site with no backup. The beat is disorientation hardening into resolve as Jude realizes rescue is not coming.

chapters.title: What Vess Carried
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. She reveals encrypted evidence that her defection was staged as bait to draw out Jude's employer's network, and that the client Jude guarded was the real target. The beat is betrayal — Jude's duty was weaponized against them from the start.

chapters.title: Shift Changes
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara traces the deletion order to a joint task force and learns the nearest border checkpoint rotates shifts in thirty-six hours — the only window when surveillance thins. She goes off-book to warn Jude. The beat is loyalty tested against institutional fear.

chapters.title: Strangers at the Wreck
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV through Jude's eyes. The survivors — a mechanic, a teenage stowaway, the wounded client — begin functioning as a unit under Jude's reluctant command. The beat is warmth emerging in crisis: the found family forming before anyone admits it.

chapters.title: The Client's Confession
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The dying client admits he sold out Vess's route to buy his own safety, forcing Jude to weigh protecting him against protecting the group. The beat is moral fracture — duty and love pulling in opposite directions for the first time openly.

chapters.title: Hunters on the Perimeter
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. A cleanup team reaches the airfield; the group scatters toward the border on foot through marshland. The stowaway is nearly taken, and Vess chooses exposure over escape to save her. The beat is terror laced with fierce tenderness — survival now means each other.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Nine
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, climax. During the shift change, Jude runs the extraction: decoy vehicles, burned credentials, Vess carried across in a maintenance convoy. Mara covers them remotely until she can't. The beat is white-knuckle sacrifice — Jude trades their entire professional existence for the crossing.

chapters.title: After the Manifest
chapters.summary: Vess's POV, resolution. Weeks later, officially nonexistent, Jude and the survivors regroup in a coastal town where Vess's evidence is released anonymously. Jude has no name left but has a family. The beat is quiet, costly peace — love won at the full price of the old life.
